text:
Robert Thomas has always been a passer first, but this is extreme: 22 shots in 17 games, and no shots at all in four of his last ten. He has 12 points, 0.65 expected goals per 60, and a scoring rate (2.06 points per 60) just under the league average for forwards. His talent range says he should be near 2.72.

There's no bad-luck excuse. St. Louis has scored 6 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, so his total is, if anything, flattered. The Blues aren't getting the Thomas who drove play last season, when Evolving-Hockey had him 20th among forwards at 2.8 wins and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 79% of his exits leaving the zone with possession.

Yahoo Sports and The Hockey News have both made the case for reuniting him with Jimmy Snuggerud and Dylan Holloway. His power-play goal at New Jersey on Nov. 5 was a start, but the Blues have gone three games without a win. Our projection still says 76 points. For that, the shots have to come back.
headline: Robert Thomas has nearly stopped shooting
